newsitem.title: USA: Culligan Water shares up as concerns wane.
newsitem.headline: Culligan Water shares up as concerns wane.

text.p: Culligan Water Technologies Inc shares traded higher Monday as investor concerns about increased competition subsided, analysts said.

"The stock's rebound is in part a reaction to weakness last week," said Walter Morris, an analyst at Robert W. Baird & Co Inc. "There was some concern (last week) about increased competition from U.S. Filter."
Last month, U.S. Filter Corp said it would acquire U.S. Water Co, a Culligan franchisee, for an undisclosed price. U.S. Water terminated its relationship with Culligan.
Culligan responded by filing a lawsuit accusing the two companies and a U.S. Water executive of violating franchise agreements with Northbrook, Illinois-based Culligan.
Richard Eastman, an analyst at Cleary Gull Reiland & McDevitt Inc, said the moves took their toll on Culligan shares.
"The stock has been soft for the last couple of weeks," he said. "(The U.S. Filter deal) got people a little skittish."
Eastman said he doesn't believe the defection, by a water distribution franchisee that made up less than one percent of Culligan's annual sales, will necessarily hurt future plans.
"The dealer distribution is a big part of (Culligan)," he said, "but they won't see any kind of mass exodus of dealers.
Baird analyst Morris added more competition won't be too much of an issue for Culligan in terms of the larger picture.
"U.S. Filter will continue to be a significant factor," he explained, "but the consumer water purification business is a $3-billion market, so there's room for a lot of players."

Culligan Monday also announced a corporate partnership with Moen Inc, a unit of American Brands Inc, that calls for Moen to incorporate Culligan water filtration assemblies in its product line. Terms were not disclosed.
Morris believes the deal is part of a recently announced effort by Culligan to expand its consumer products line.
"One of the key strengths Culligan has is this great consumer trade name," Morris said. "(The Moen deal) is part of a plan to leverage that name."
